headline: Baffin Island Backcountry Permits and Safety
reservation: All hikers and climbers must attend a mandatory safety orientation and register at the Parks Canada office in Pangnirtung or Qikiqtarjuaq. Backcountry camping fees apply, and a reservation system may be in effect for peak summer slots. Check the official Parks Canada Nunavut site for current polar bear safety requirements and river crossing updates.

days.title: Gateway to the Arctic Circle

stops.name: Pangnirtung Fiord
stops.detail: Take a local boat charter through the dramatic fiord to the trailhead at Overlord.

stops.name: Ulu Peak
stops.detail: Observe the distinctive shape of this peak, which resembles a traditional Inuit knife, marking the entrance to the pass.

days.driving: Allow 1–2 hours for boat transfer; conditions vary based on low tide and ice floes.
days.note: Boats cannot land at Overlord during extreme low tides; check local tide tables.

days.title: The Granite Giants

stops.name: Mount Asgard
stops.detail: View the twin flat-topped granite towers, a world-renowned landmark for technical climbers.

stops.name: Thor Peak
stops.detail: Witness the world's greatest vertical drop at 1,250 meters on this sheer granite face.

days.driving: Hike duration varies by fitness; allow a full day for the trek to the Thor Lake area.
days.note: River crossings can be dangerous; plan to cross in the early morning when glacial melt is lowest.

days.title: Crossing the Arctic Circle

stops.name: Summit Lake
stops.detail: Reach the high point of the Akshayuk Pass where the Arctic Circle is officially crossed.

stops.name: Schwartzenbach Falls
stops.detail: View the cascading meltwater against the backdrop of the Penny Ice Cap's edge.

days.driving: Walking only; travel across boulder fields and glacial moraine requires significant time.
days.note: High winds in the pass can reach gale force; secure all gear and monitor weather shifts.

intel.title: Fiord Boat Transfers
intel.text: Access to the trailheads at Overlord or North Pangnirtung Fiord requires hiring local outfitters for boat transport. Ice conditions can block these routes well into July.

intel.title: Satellite Dependency
intel.text: No cellular service exists beyond the hamlets. Parks Canada recommends carrying a satellite messaging device for daily check-ins and emergency alerts.

intel.title: Hamlet Supplies
intel.text: Purchase naphtha or white gas at the local Co-op or Northern Store in Pangnirtung. Air carriers prohibit transporting these fuels on passenger flights from Iqaluit.

intel.title: Melt Season
intel.text: The hiking season is typically July to late August. Earlier travel involves hazardous river crossings and lingering snow bridge risks in the pass.

intel.title: No Road Network
intel.text: There are no roads to the park or within it. Logistics involve walking from the hamlet or utilizing boat/snowmobile transfers depending on the season.

plan.arrival: Fly from YFB to Pangnirtung, check in at the Parks Canada visitor center for your mandatory briefing, and meet your boat outfitter at the municipal wharf.
plan.vehicle: No road vehicles are suitable; travel is by foot, boat, or seasonal snowmobile only.
plan.goldenHour: Mount Thor’s west face during the late evening light of the Arctic summer.
